sentences.text: Heard on the question of admission.
Also heard o n I.A. No. 5630/2022, which is first application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail filed under Section 389(1) of Cr.P.C. on behalf of appellant-Vikram Kol.

The appellant has been convicted vide judgment dated 23/03/2022 passed by Special Judge (Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012), Umaria in Special Case No. 20/2018 for commission of offence punishable under Sections 363, 366, 376(2)(Dha) and 376(2)(Jha) of IPC and under Section 5(Tha)/6 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 and sentenced to undergo RI for 3 years, 10 years and 10 years and to pay fine of Rs.1000/- for each offence respectively with usual default stipulations.

entities.text: Special Judge (Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012), Umaria
entities.label: COURT

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the trial Court has not properly appreciated the evidence in its proper perspective and committed grave error in convicting the appellant for aforesaid offence.
There is no evidence available on record to connect the appellant with the alleged offence.

There are fair chances of success of this appeal and final hearing of same will take considerable time, therefore, if remaining custodial sentence has not been suspended, then the appeal filed by appellant may turn infructuous.
Under these circumstances, learned counsel for appellant prays for suspension of jail sentence and release of the appellant on bail till the final disposal of the appeal.

In support of his contentions, learned counsel for appellant has placed reliance on judgments of Hon'ble Apex Court delivered in Criminal Appeal Nos. 635/2020 &
1898/2023 as well as in various orders passed by this Court in Cr.A. Nos. 5518/2022, 6257/2021 and 349/2013.

sentences.text:
O n the other hand, learned Government Advocate for the respondent/State has opposed the prayer by contending that at the time of alleged incident, the prosecutrix was minor and aforesaid fact is well established by statements of Banshilal Rautel (PW 1) and Dr. Bolga Kaithwar (PW 5),
Prosecutrix (PW 6), father of prosecutrix (PW 3), mother of prosecutrix (PW 7) and sister of prosecutrix (PW 2) have fully supported the prosecution case.
Hence, he pays for dismissal of aforesaid application.

Looking to the aforesaid facts and circumstances of the case and role attributed to the appellant in commission of aforesaid offence and age of the prosecutrix at the time of alleged incident and other material available on record against appellant, in the considered opinion of this Court, at this stage no case is made out for suspension of custodial sentence and grant of bail to appellant.

Accordingly,
I.A. No.5630/2022 is hereby dismissed.
So far as the judgments relied by learned counsel for appellant is concerned they are not applicable in the facts and circumstances of present case.

List the appeal for final hearing in due course (ROOPESH CHANDRA VARSHNEY) JUDGE skt Vikram Kol vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 18 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/75715800/
